references.text: In both Isaiah and Luke, trees that do not bear good fruit are used as a metaphor for people who do not live righteous lives, and in both passages it is mentioned that these trees will be cut down.
Similar to Isaiah, Jeremiah also uses the image of trees that do not bear fruit as a metaphor for people who do not follow God's ways, and it is noted that these trees will be removed.

In Matthew, as in Luke, there is a warning that any tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire, which underscores the importance of living a life that bears good fruit.
